BridgePath

From: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing comp and packaging details — BridgePath RFP follow-up

Kim / Connor / Marissa,

Quick model and recommended offer below (high-level, conservative):

1) Base price-match (run-rate)
- Incumbent reported effective rate: $0.000045 / token (avg) across gen + embeddings per their sheet.
- Proposed Redwood match: $0.000045 / token for first 12 months on a 12-month commitment.
- Condition: match applies to equivalent served model tier and not to enterprise-only variants (we'll map model parity).

2) Migration & pilot package
- Pilot credit: $25k credit valid for 90 days (covers proof-of-concept traffic — encourages immediate usage).
- Migration credit: $60k one-time credit applied to first invoice as service credit (offsets data egress + onboarding).
- Dedicated migration support: 5 engineering days (remote), plus optional paid on-site (T&E) if required — goal is 2-4 week cutover.

3) Packaging & SLA recommendations
- Offer A (Cost-sensitive): Hosted API with caching and quantization profile applied; includes 12-month price-match and pilot + migration credits above; standard 99.5% API SLA.
- Offer B (Ops-sensitive): Dedicated capacity reserved for BridgePath with 6-week lead + 99.9% SLA and two-week canary window; adds $X/mo baseline (we'll calculate exact base given their usage).
- Offer C (Regulated): Private deployment (VPC) — longer lead, managed support, potential additional engineering days and a higher baseline fee; price-match can be offered on per-token component but not on fixed monthly reservation.

4) Constraints and callouts
- Price-match excludes third-party managed services fees (egress, cloud infra) — we can include estimates but these are often outside Redwood unit pricing.
- Data retention: Redwood retains audit logs for 90 days by default; extension to 1 year is available as an add-on.
- Model parity: We'll commit to an agreed mapping between our verified model profile and incumbent model family; any material quality regression must be surfaced in 30-day eval.

5) Next steps (internal)
- Connor: run the TCO model in the attached spreadsheet to compute monthly base number for Offer A and Offer B (use incumbents usage profile).
- Marissa: create redlined term-sheet (I can draft standard concession language — include rollback protections).
- Kimberly: I'll assemble the one-page comparison and a proposed term-sheet v1.

I'll drop the numbers in the spreadsheet and share updated term-sheet by EOD Friday.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Jordan,

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the detail. The price-match + pilot/ migration credits look like a direction we can present. A few items before we escalate to CFO:  

- Can you send a formal term-sheet (PDF) with the Offer A baseline numbers filled in (monthly run-rate and per-token rate) and the credits called out line-by-line?
- Procurement would like a 30-day pilot window with clear evaluation KPIs and an explicit rollback clause if latency or accuracy regressions exceed thresholds.
- We will need one-year extended audit log retention in writing (cost acceptable as add-on).

If you can return an updated term-sheet and a DocuSign link by Monday morning we can schedule a pricing review with the CFO on Tue. Also, could you increase the pilot credit to $35k — that will cover ramping their internal pilot usage. If not possible, give us the rationale briefly (we'll take it to procurement).

Thanks,
Alyssa
